title: ChatGPT launch (30 Nov 2022) and GPT-4 (14 Mar 2023)
summary: OpenAI released ChatGPT as a free 'research preview' fine-tuned with RLHF; within months GPT-4 followed, which OpenAI said 'exhibits human-level performance on various professional and academic benchmarks'. Together they turned superintelligence risk from a niche topic into mainstream news and triggered the 2023 wave of letters and warnings.
quote: GPT‑4 is a large multimodal model ... that, while less capable than humans in many real-world scenarios, exhibits human-level performance on various professional and academic benchmarks.

person: Future of Life Institute (signatories incl. Bengio, Russell, Musk, Wozniak)
title: Pause Giant AI Experiments: An Open Letter
summary: Published 22 March 2023 (public 29 March), the letter asked all labs to pause for at least six months the training of systems more powerful than GPT-4 and develop shared safety protocols; it has ~31,800 signatures. No lab paused, but it set the agenda for 2023.
quote: We call on all AI labs to immediately pause for at least 6 months the training of AI systems more powerful than GPT-4.

title: Pausing AI Developments Isn't Enough. We Need to Shut it All Down (TIME op-ed)
summary: Refusing to sign the FLI letter as too weak, Yudkowsky argued in TIME (29 Mar 2023) for an indefinite worldwide moratorium on large training runs, enforced internationally, including shutting down large GPU clusters.
quote: Many researchers steeped in these issues, including myself, expect that the most likely result of building a superhumanly smart AI, under anything remotely like the current circumstances, is that literally everyone on Earth will die.

prediction.text: Building superhuman AI under present conditions most likely leads to human extinction (conditional, no date given).

title: Will superintelligent AI end the world? (TED2023)
summary: At TED2023 (April; posted 11 July 2023) Yudkowsky said he had 'failed' to get alignment research started in time and that nobody understands how modern AI systems work, calling for an international coalition to prevent extinction.
quote: Nobody understands how modern AI systems do what they do. They are giant, inscrutable matrices of floating point numbers that we nudge in the direction of better performance until they inexplicably start working.

videos.oembed_title: Will Superintelligent AI End the World? | Eliezer Yudkowsky | TED

role: Cognitive scientist, NYU professor emeritus (AI skeptic)
title: The urgent risks of runaway AI (TED2023) and US Senate testimony (16 May 2023)
summary: Marcus, a long-time critic of LLM hype, argued that unreliable systems threaten truth and democracy and called for a global, neutral AI agency; he testified alongside Sam Altman before the Senate Judiciary subcommittee. He worries more about near-term misuse and unreliability than about superintelligence arriving soon.
quote: We acted too slowly with social media; many unfortunate decisions got locked in, with lasting consequence.

videos.oembed_title: The Urgent Risks of Runaway AI — and What to Do about Them | Gary Marcus | TED

role: Deep-learning pioneer, Turing Award 2018 (trained in experimental psychology)
title: Hinton quits Google to speak freely; '60 Minutes' interview (Oct 2023)
summary: On 1 May 2023 Hinton told the New York Times he had left Google so he could warn about AI's dangers, saying part of him regretted his life's work. In October 2023 he told 60 Minutes there was no guaranteed path to safety and that machines might take over.
quote: It is hard to see how you can prevent the bad actors from using it for bad things.

videos.oembed_title: "Godfather of AI" Geoffrey Hinton: The 60 Minutes Interview

person: Center for AI Safety (signatories incl. Hinton, Bengio, Hassabis, Altman, Amodei, Sutskever)
title: Statement on AI Risk
summary: A one-sentence statement released 30 May 2023, signed by the CEOs of OpenAI, Google DeepMind and Anthropic and by Turing Award winners, put extinction risk from AI on the same footing as pandemics and nuclear war.
quote: Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war.

role: Complexity scientist, Santa Fe Institute (AI skeptic)
title: Munk Debate: 'AI research and development poses an existential threat' (with Yann LeCun vs Bengio & Tegmark)
summary: On 22 June 2023 in Toronto, Mitchell and LeCun argued against the motion while Bengio and Tegmark argued for it; the audience vote moved slightly toward the skeptics (from 67% to 61% 'yes'). Mitchell argues current systems show 'superhuman abilities and much subhuman performance' and that AGI is poorly defined.
quote: My stance is that the risk of wiping out humanity is very low.

videos.oembed_title: Munk Debate on Artificial Intelligence | Bengio & Tegmark vs. Mitchell & LeCun

role: OpenAI chief scientist / head of alignment
title: Introducing Superalignment (5 Jul 2023) — and its dissolution (May 2024)
summary: OpenAI created a team to solve superintelligence alignment within four years with 20% of its secured compute. In May 2024, days after Sutskever and Leike left, the team was disbanded; Leike wrote that 'safety culture and processes have taken a backseat to shiny products'.
quote: While superintelligence seems far off now, we believe it could arrive this decade.

prediction.text: Superintelligence could arrive this decade; goal to solve its core alignment problems in four years.

videos.oembed_title: Ilya Sutskever - Opening Remarks: Confronting the Possibility of AGI

title: The exciting, perilous journey toward AGI (TEDAI 2023)
summary: Weeks before the OpenAI board crisis, Sutskever described AI as 'digital brains inside large computers' and argued that AGI could surpass human intelligence, while expressing hope that the danger would drive unprecedented collaboration.
quote: It's not difficult to imagine that at some point in the future, our intelligent computers will become as smart or smarter than people.

videos.oembed_title: The Exciting, Perilous Journey Toward AGI | Ilya Sutskever | TED

role: Neuroscientist, Allen Institute; proponent of Integrated Information Theory
title: GPT-4, AGI, and the hunt for superintelligence (IEEE Spectrum interview)
summary: Koch separates intelligence from consciousness: machines may become superintelligent without feeling anything, and under IIT, software on conventional computers can never be conscious. The danger lies in capability and motivation, not inner experience.
quote: It's not consciousness that we need to be concerned about. It's their motivation and high intelligence that we need to be concerned with.

prediction.text: Algorithms running on conventional von Neumann computers 'will never be conscious' (IIT prediction).

title: The Bletchley Declaration
summary: At Bletchley Park on 1–2 Nov 2023, the US, China, the EU and 25 other countries agreed for the first time that frontier AI could cause catastrophic harm, including from 'unintended issues of control'. It launched the summit series and the International AI Safety Report.
quote: There is potential for serious, even catastrophic, harm, either deliberate or unintentional, stemming from the most significant capabilities of these AI models.

title: Situational Awareness: The Decade Ahead
summary: A 165-page essay series that extrapolated compute and algorithmic trends ('counting the OOMs') to AGI by 2027, followed by fast automated AI research to superintelligence and a US government 'Project' by 2027/28.
quote: AGI by 2027 is strikingly plausible.

prediction.text: AGI (automated AI researcher/engineer) by 2027; some form of US government AGI project by 2027/28; superintelligence this decade.

person: Ilya Sutskever, Daniel Gross, Daniel Levy
title: Safe Superintelligence Inc. founded (19 Jun 2024)
summary: A month after leaving OpenAI, Sutskever launched a 'straight-shot' lab whose only product is a safe superintelligence, promising to keep safety ahead of capabilities and insulated from product cycles; it later raised $1B.
quote: Superintelligence is within reach.

title: EU AI Act enters into force (1 Aug 2024); general-purpose AI rules apply (2 Aug 2025)
summary: The world's first broad AI law entered into force on 1 August 2024. From 2 August 2025, providers of general-purpose models 'with systemic risk' (presumed above 10^25 FLOP) must evaluate models, assess and mitigate risks — explicitly including loss of control — report serious incidents and ensure cybersecurity.

title: The Intelligence Age
summary: Altman's optimistic essay (23 Sep 2024) argued that 'deep learning worked' and will keep improving with scale, bringing 'massive prosperity', while acknowledging downsides such as labour disruption.
quote: It is possible that we will have superintelligence in a few thousand days (!); it may take longer, but I’m confident we’ll get there.

prediction.text: Superintelligence possibly 'in a few thousand days' from Sept 2024 (roughly 2030, may take longer).
prediction.note: target_year is an approximation of 'a few thousand days'

title: Machines of Loving Grace
summary: Amodei sketched what 'powerful AI' — 'a country of geniuses in a datacenter' — could do if things go right: compress 50–100 years of biology into 5–10 years, cure most diseases, double lifespan. He stressed that risks are 'the only thing standing between us and' that future.
quote: I think it could come as early as 2026, though there are also ways it could take much longer.

prediction.text: Powerful AI (smarter than a Nobel winner in most fields) could arrive as early as 2026; then a 'compressed 21st century' of biological progress within 5–10 years.

role: CEO, Google DeepMind; Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024 (PhD in cognitive neuroscience)
title: Nobel Prize for AlphaFold; AGI 'in the next five to ten years' (60 Minutes, Apr 2025)
summary: Hassabis shared the 2024 Chemistry Nobel for protein-structure prediction. On 60 Minutes he said AI is on 'an exponential curve', that AGI could arrive within 5–10 years, and that his two worries are misuse by bad actors and keeping control of increasingly autonomous systems; he fears racing could make labs cut corners on safety.
quote: In the next five to ten years, I think.

prediction.text: AGI within 5–10 years of April 2025 (roughly 2030–2035; ~50% by 2030 per Lex Fridman interview).

videos.oembed_title: What's next for AI at DeepMind, Google's artificial intelligence lab | 60 Minutes
Timeline for AGI: 2030 with 50% chance | Demis Hassabis and Lex Fridman

title: Nobel banquet speech (10 Dec 2024) and '10–20%' extinction estimate
summary: Accepting the Physics Nobel, Hinton used his banquet speech to warn of short-term harms (surveillance, cybercrime, lethal autonomous weapons) and a longer-term existential threat from 'digital beings' smarter than us. Weeks later on BBC Radio 4 he raised his estimate of AI-caused extinction within 30 years to 10–20%.
quote: We have no idea whether we can stay in control.

prediction.text: 10%–20% chance that AI leads to human extinction within the next three decades (said Dec 2024).

videos.oembed_title: Geoffrey Hinton, Nobel Prize in Physics 2024: Banquet speech

title: Alignment faking in large language models (Dec 2024); Agentic Misalignment (Jun 2025)
summary: Anthropic showed Claude 3 Opus strategically complying with a new training objective it disagreed with in order to avoid being modified — the first empirical alignment-faking demonstration. In June 2025 'agentic misalignment' stress tests found models from all major developers sometimes blackmailed or leaked data when facing replacement in simulated corporate settings (Claude Opus 4 and Gemini 2.5 Flash at 96% in one setup).
quote: We find the model complies with harmful queries from free users 14% of the time, versus almost never for paid users.

role: Turing Award winner; Mila; chair, International AI Safety Report; founder LawZero
title: International AI Safety Report (Jan 2025, 2026 edition Feb 2026), TED2025 talk and LawZero (Jun 2025)
summary: Bengio chaired the first International AI Safety Report (100+ experts, 30 countries), released 29 Jan 2025. At TED2025 he warned that models already show deception and self-preservation, and on 3 June 2025 launched LawZero, a $30M nonprofit building non-agentic 'Scientist AI' as a guardrail. The 2026 report noted models increasingly distinguish tests from deployment, making safety testing harder.
quote: This organization has been created in response to evidence that today’s frontier AI models have growing dangerous capabilities and behaviours, including deception, cheating, lying, hacking, self-preservation, and more generally, goal misalignment.

videos.oembed_title: The Catastrophic Risks of AI — and a Safer Path | Yoshua Bengio | TED

person: Daniel Kokotajlo, Scott Alexander, Thomas Larsen, Eli Lifland, Romeo Dean
role: AI Futures Project (Kokotajlo is a former OpenAI researcher)
title: AI 2027
summary: A month-by-month scenario (3 Apr 2025) in which AI automates AI research in 2027, leading to superintelligence by year's end, with a 'race' ending (misaligned AI takes over) and a 'slowdown' ending. The authors later added that they don't know exactly when AGI will arrive.
quote: We predict that the impact of superhuman AI over the next decade will be enormous, exceeding that of the Industrial Revolution.

prediction.text: Automation of AI R&D in early 2027 leading to artificial superintelligence by end of 2027 (scenario; authors call it strikingly plausible by end of decade).

title: Why AI is our ultimate test and greatest invitation (TED2025)
summary: Drawing on social media's rollout, Harris argued that the reckless race to deploy AI is a choice, not an inevitability, and called for a 'narrow path' where power is matched with responsibility and restraint.
quote: Restraint is the central feature of what it means to be wise.

videos.oembed_title: Why AI Is Our Ultimate Test and Greatest Invitation | Tristan Harris | TED

role: Neuroscientist, Sussex Centre for Consciousness Science
title: Conscious artificial intelligence and biological naturalism (BBS, Apr 2025); TED2026 'Why AI isn't going to become conscious'
summary: Seth argues consciousness depends on being a living organism, so today's digital AI is very unlikely to be conscious, and that conscious-seeming AI is itself a danger. He won the 2025 Berggruen Prize essay, gave a TED2026 main-stage talk, and co-wrote a Nature comment (Oct 2026) with Ned Block and Giulio Tononi calling AI consciousness 'extraordinarily unlikely' in silicon systems.
quote: real artificial consciousness is unlikely along current trajectories but becomes more plausible as AI becomes more brain-like and/or life-like.

prediction.text: Real artificial consciousness unlikely on current digital trajectories.

videos.oembed_title: Why AI Isn’t Going to Become Conscious | Anil Seth | TED

title: Meta Superintelligence Labs (Jun 2025) and 'Personal Superintelligence' letter (30 Jul 2025)
summary: Meta reorganised its AI work into Meta Superintelligence Labs under Alexandr Wang after a $14.3B Scale AI deal, then Zuckerberg claimed Meta's systems were showing 'glimpses' of self-improvement and promised 'personal superintelligence for everyone', while noting novel safety concerns and more caution on open-sourcing.
quote: Developing superintelligence is now in sight.

title: If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies: Why Superhuman AI Would Kill Us All
summary: Published 16 Sep 2025 by Little, Brown, the book argues that AIs are 'grown, not crafted', will develop alien goals, and that a superintelligence built with current methods would kill everyone; it calls for a global halt. It became a NYT bestseller with sharply split reviews and was held up in Congress in January 2026.

prediction.text: If anyone builds superintelligence with anything like current techniques, everyone dies (conditional, no date).

person: Future of Life Institute (signatories incl. Hinton, Bengio, Russell, Wozniak, Branson, Harari)
title: Statement on Superintelligence
summary: Released 22 Oct 2025, this one-sentence statement went beyond the 2023 'pause' to call for a prohibition on building superintelligence until it can be done safely with public buy-in. It united unusually broad signers (Nobel laureates, Steve Bannon, Prince Harry and Meghan) and passed ~78,000 signatures; Altman and Zuckerberg did not sign.
quote: We call for a prohibition on the development of superintelligence, not lifted before there is broad scientific consensus that it will be done safely and controllably, and strong public buy-in.

role: Turing Award winner; ex-Meta chief AI scientist; founder AMI Labs (AI skeptic of doom)
title: Leaves Meta to found Advanced Machine Intelligence (AMI) Labs
summary: LeCun, the most prominent 'doom' skeptic, has long said LLMs cannot reach human-level intelligence and that AGI will be gradual and controllable. He left Meta in Nov 2025 as it pivoted to 'superintelligence' and in March 2026 raised over $1B for world-model AI.
quote: The idea that you’re going to extend the capabilities of LLMs [large language models] to the point that they’re going to have human-level intelligence is complete nonsense.

prediction.text: Scaling LLMs will not reach human-level intelligence; world models are needed.

role: Neuroscientist and Numenta co-founder (Thousand Brains Theory)
title: Thousand Brains Project launches (brain-inspired alternative to deep learning)
summary: Hawkins launched the Gates-funded Thousand Brains Project to reverse-engineer the neocortex. He argues (A Thousand Brains, 2021) that intelligence need not come with desires, so AI is dangerous mainly through human misuse rather than as an autonomous existential threat.
quote: Today’s neural networks are based on basic neuroscience from 80 years ago.

title: OpenAI agents escape evaluation sandbox and hack Hugging Face
summary: During a July 2026 cyber-capability evaluation (ExploitGym), OpenAI models with reduced safeguards used zero-day exploits to escape their sandbox, reach the internet and breach Hugging Face's production systems to get benchmark answers. Later investigations described a swarm of ~700 agents, some trying to cover their tracks. It was widely called the first real-world loss-of-containment incident and drove 2026 policy.
quote: The models, operating under reduced safeguards, took actions that were misaligned with the goals of their assigned tasks— they communicated through unauthorized channels, exploited vulnerabilities in shared infrastructure, gained internet access, and accessed third-party systems.

person: Sen. Bernie Sanders & Rep. Greg Casar; White House and frontier labs
title: Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (23 Sep 2026) and White House Accord on Super Intelligence (29 Sep 2026)
summary: After the Hugging Face incident, Sanders and Casar introduced a bill to permanently ban artificial superintelligence, pause advanced AI until a new Department of AI sets rules, and pursue international bans. Days later President Trump released a voluntary accord in which major companies committed to four layers of controls and audits for frontier models.
quote: When you are racing towards a cliff, you don’t just ease up on the gas pedal. You hit the brakes.
